problems.title: Rationalize three conjugate denominators
problems.question: Evaluate 1/(√5−2)+4/(3+√5)+8/(√5+1).
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: (u−v)(u+v)=u²−v².
steps: The terms simplify respectively to √5+2,3−√5,2√5−2. Their sum is 3+2√5.

problems.title: A line avoiding quadrant two
problems.question: Which listed a makes y=(a−1)x+4−a avoid quadrant II?
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Quadrant II requires x<0,y>0.
steps: If a≤1, the nonpositive slope and positive intercept force some points into II. For a>1 the line avoids II exactly when intercept 4−a≤0, giving a≥4.

problems.title: Percentage of sunny days
problems.question: June had 24 sunny and 6 cloudy days. What percentage were sunny?
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Percentage=100×part/total.
steps: Total=30 days. Sunny fraction=24/30=0.8, or 80%.

problems.title: A parallel line through one point
problems.question: A=(2,3),B=(4,5),C=(3,3). Find the line through A parallel to BC.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
steps: Through A, y−3=2(x−2), hence y=2x−1.

problems.title: Greatest integer below a radical
problems.question: Find the greatest integer smaller than 3√7.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: (3√7)²=63, between 7²=49 and 8²=64.
steps: Both sides are positive, so 7<3√7<8. The requested integer is 7.

problems.title: Two successive fractional withdrawals
problems.question: A container has 1200 litres. Remove 1/6 of it and then 3/10 of the remainder. How much remains?
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Multiply by retained fractions 5/6 and 7/10.

problems.title: Order three powers of a negative fraction
problems.question: a=−0.8. Order a⁴,a⁵,a⁶ increasingly.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Odd powers are negative, even powers positive; powers of a magnitude below 1 shrink with increasing exponent.
steps: a⁵ is negative. Between the positives, a⁶<a⁴. Therefore a⁵<a⁶<a⁴.

problems.title: Parallel triangle cross-sections
problems.question: MN and KT are parallel to AC in triangle ABC, with MN:KT:AC=2:5:9. Find BN:NT:TC.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Similar-triangle side fractions match their parallel-base fractions.
steps: BN/BC=2/9 and BT/BC=5/9. Thus NT/BC=3/9 and TC/BC=4/9.
The ratio is 2:3:4.

problems.title: Successive percentage gifts
problems.question: A grandmother gives away 20%, then 10% of the remainder, then 25% of the new remainder. What percentage remains?
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Multiply retained proportions 0.8,0.9,0.75.
steps: The retained fraction is 0.8×0.9×0.75=0.54, or 54%.

problems.title: A telescoping product
problems.question: Evaluate (1·3/2²)(2·4/3²)…(98·100/99²).
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Each factor at k=2,…,99 is [(k−1)/k][(k+1)/k].
steps: The first product telescopes to 1/99 and the second to 100/2. Multiply to get 50/99.

problems.title: Read the tortoise-and-hare distance graph
problems.question: Choose the graph showing a steady tortoise, a faster hare who sleeps, and the tortoise reaching the finish first.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: On a distance-time graph, constant speed is a straight rising line and sleeping is a horizontal segment.
steps: Graph D shows the tortoise’s straight line reaching the same finishing distance earlier. The hare’s graph rises, stays horizontal while sleeping, then rises steeply and reaches that distance later.
The other displayed graphs show an inconsistent finish order, a tie, or no horizontal sleeping segment.

problems.title: Multiply numbers either side of a thousand
problems.question: Evaluate 1003×997.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: (a+b)(a−b)=a²−b².

problems.title: Sum parallel segments inside a right triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has legs 6,8. Seven equally spaced interior hypotenuse points have segments parallel to the longer leg, ending on the other leg. Find their length sum.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Similar triangles make the segment lengths 8k/8 for k=1,…,7.
steps: The lengths are 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 in some order. Their sum is 7×8/2=28.

problems.title: Equal perimeters in an isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: ABCD is an isosceles trapezoid, BC parallel AD, and BH its altitude to AD. Perimeter ABCH=12. Find perimeter DCH.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Equal legs AB=CD; base geometry gives HD=BC+AH.
steps: ABCH perimeter is AB+BC+CH+AH. Replace AB by CD and BC+AH by HD.
This is CD+CH+HD, exactly the DCH perimeter.

problems.title: A square of a bounded linear expression
problems.question: 1<a<2 and 3<b<4. Bound Y=(2a−b)².
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
steps: The interval contains zero, which is attained for example at a=1.75,b=3.5. Squaring gives 0≤Y<4; the upper bound is approached but not reached.

problems.title: Radius from a chord point’s power
problems.question: A chord is 6.5 long. M on it is distance 4 from the centre and splits the chord in ratio 9:4. Find radius.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: For an interior point, MA·MB=R²−OM².
steps: The pieces are 4.5 and 2, with product 9. Thus R²=16+9=25 and R=5.

problems.title: Move a nonnegative factor into a square root
problems.question: Simplify −x√(−x) on its real domain.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Domain x≤0 makes −x≥0; c√d=√(c²d) for c≥0,d≥0.
steps: The expression is √[x²(−x)]=√(−x³), nonnegative throughout the domain.

problems.title: Rectangle inscribed against a right-isosceles hypotenuse
problems.question: An isosceles right triangle has hypotenuse 42 cm. Rectangle ABCD has A,D on it and B,C on the legs; AB:BC=2:3. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: At perpendicular distance h from the hypotenuse, the parallel triangle cross-section has length 42−2h.
steps: Let AB=h and BC=w. Then w=42−2h and h:w=2:3 gives w=3h/2.
42=7h/2 gives h=12,w=18. Perimeter=2(12+18)=60 cm.

problems.title: Model two workers’ times
problems.question: Two workers together finish in 12 days. The first completes half the job alone, then the second one third, taking 20 days altogether. Give a system for their solo times x,y.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Rates add; time to complete a fraction equals that fraction times solo time.
steps: Together, 1/x+1/y=1/12. Sequential times are x/2 and y/3, giving x/2+y/3=20.

problems.title: Bisectors of unequal supplementary angles
problems.question: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. Find the angle between bisectors of two differently sized nonstraight angles.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: The two distinct angle sizes are theta and 180°−theta.
steps: Their bisectors differ by half the sum: theta/2+(180−theta)/2=90°. Parallel copies preserve these directions.

problems.title: A large power of a sixth root of unity
problems.question: z=(1+√3i)/2. Find z²⁰²².
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: z=cos(π/3)+i sin(π/3); use De Moivre’s formula.
steps: 2022=6×337, so the angle after exponentiation is 337 full turns. Thus the result is 1.

problems.title: A quadratic equation over complex numbers
problems.question: Which listed z satisfies z(z−2)=−2?
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
steps: The roots are z=1±i. The listed value 1+i is valid.

problems.title: A listed cube root of a pure imaginary number
problems.question: Which listed z satisfies z³=8i?
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: 8i has modulus 8 and argument π/2; its cube roots have modulus 2 and arguments π/6+2kπ/3.
steps: The three roots are √3+i,−√3+i,−2i. The listed i−√3 is the second one.

problems.title: A similarity from an angle on a divided side
problems.question: D lies on BC with BAD=BCA and BD:DC=2:1. Find AD:AC.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Triangles BAD and BCA are similar: their B angles agree and BAD=BCA.
steps: The correspondence gives AD/AC=BA/BC=BD/BA. Hence (BA/BC)²=BD/BC=2/3.
The positive length ratio is √(2/3)=√6/3.

problems.title: Perimeter of a midpoint quadrilateral
problems.question: A quadrilateral has diagonals 6,8. Find the perimeter formed by its consecutive side midpoints.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Triangle midsegments are parallel to and half the length of a diagonal.
steps: The midpoint parallelogram has alternating sides 3 and 4. Its perimeter is 2(3+4)=14.

problems.title: Distance between two equal-side incircle contacts
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 15 and base 10. Find the distance between incircle contact points on the equal sides.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Tangent length from the apex=s−base; use similarity with the original triangle.
steps: The semiperimeter is 20, so each apex-to-contact length is 10. The contact-point triangle has scale 10/15=2/3.
The contact chord parallel to the base has length 10×2/3=20/3.

problems.title: Four consecutive odd integers
problems.question: Which of 16,40,72,100 cannot be the sum of four consecutive odd integers?
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
steps: Every such sum is divisible by 8, and every multiple of 8 is obtained for an integer k. Among the choices only 100 is not divisible by 8.

problems.title: A pair of fractional linear inequalities
problems.question: Solve (2/5)x−1/3<(1/5)x+5/3 and (x−2)/3≥(x−6)/6.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Multiply by positive common denominators.
steps: The first simplifies to x<10. The second becomes 2x−4≥x−6, or x≥−2.
The intersection is [−2,10).

problems.title: Clock angle at three forty
problems.question: Find the smaller clock-hand angle at 15:40.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Hour angle=30h+0.5m; minute angle=6m.
steps: The hour hand is at 90+20=110° and the minute hand at 240°. The smaller difference is 130°.

problems.title: A reciprocal identity
problems.question: x−1/x=3. Evaluate (x⁴+3x²+1)/x².
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
steps: x²+1/x²=9+2=11. The requested expression adds 3, giving 14.

problems.title: Similar triangles in a parallelogram
problems.question: M lies on AD,K on CD, with ABM=CBK,AM=4,CK=3. Parallelogram perimeter is 70. Find DM,DK.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Triangles ABM and CBK are similar, since BAM=BCK and the given B angles agree.
steps: AB/BC=AM/CK=4/3. Since AB+BC=35, the sides are AB=20,BC=AD=15.

problems.title: Distance between midpoints of separated subsegments
problems.question: On AB, M lies inside AN and N inside AB. AM:MN=2:3,AN:NB=10:3. Midpoints of AM and NB are distance 10 cm apart. Find AB.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Use a common ratio unit: AM=4t,MN=6t,NB=3t.
steps: From A=0 the positions are M=4t,N=10t,B=13t. The two midpoints are at 2t and 11.5t.
Their separation is 9.5t=10, so t=20/19. Therefore AB=13t=260/19 cm.

problems.title: Revenue from two discounts
problems.question: A farmer expected revenue a from 1200 kg. One third is sold at 10% discount and two thirds at 20% discount. Find actual revenue.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: Weight each original-revenue share by its retained price fraction.
steps: The retained total fraction is (1/3)0.9+(2/3)0.8=3/10+8/15=5/6.
The actual revenue is 5a/6.

problems.title: A moving interval whose integer sum is zero
problems.question: Find all real a for which the sum of all integers in [a,a+199.2] is zero.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: The interval contains 199 or 200 consecutive integers. A nonempty consecutive-integer sum is zero exactly when its endpoints are opposites.
steps: An even number of consecutive integers cannot have integer endpoints opposite one another. Thus there must be 199 integers, namely −99 through 99.
Require ceil(a)=−99 and floor(a+199.2)=99. These mean −100<a≤−99 and −100.2≤a<−99.2.
The intersection is −100<a<−99.2. Neither endpoint works because it adds one unbalanced end integer.

problems.title: Two parallelogram bisectors meeting outside
problems.question: Angle bisectors from A,D of parallelogram ABCD meet outside it. Their intersections K,M with BC lie on that side. BM is 30% of the perimeter and BC=3. Find AB.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as exact formulas, calculate, and check the result.
formulas: The bisector from D gives CM=CD=AB, using parallel-side angles.
steps: Let AB=s. Then BM=3−s and perimeter=2(3+s). The condition is 3−s=0.3×2(3+s).
1.2=1.6s gives s=3/4. It makes both side intersections interior and the bisector intersection outside as stated.
